study_identification.author_journal_year: Wu et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification.title: Normative modeling analysis reveals corpus callosum volume changes in early and mid-to-late first episode major depression

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate CC (sub)volume differences between first episode MDD patients and age and gender matched never-depressed healthy controls using normative modeling.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: One-sample t-test on the resulting z-scores of first episode MDD patients was then performed to determine the statistical significance of the mean deviation (z-scores). To evaluate the effects of depression severity, we computed three separate Spearman correlations between the HAMD scores and CC (sub)volume z-scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: CC (sub)volume differences in early versus mid-to-late onset first episode MDD were revealed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Relative to the norms established by the healthy controls, first-episode MDD patients displayed CC volume (z-score) reductions in the entire CC (including the body), as did mid-to-late-onset first-episode MDD patients (age ≥ 45 y). In early-onset first-episode MDD patients (age ≤ 44 y), depression severity symptoms were related to volume increases in the entire CC, as well as the body and splenium.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: No data on depressive episode duration. Relatively small sample size for mid-to-late first-episode MDD patients. All recruitment sites were in Asia (China). The split between first and late onset first depressive episode should be considered as an arbitrary choice. Other factors such as cognitive information, specific depressive characteristics, or history or current suicide attempts were not included. Regarding CC subvolume parcellation, we used only three CC subvolumes, but other parcellation atlases of the CC are available.

general_notes.general_notes: The study used a large dataset from the REST-meta-MDD Consortium. The use of normative modeling with hierarchical Bayesian regression to account for site effects is a key feature of this study.
